correctness.rationale: Exact orbit-space basis and translation identity; singular locus localized to nonsingular conic q=0; exact F2[t] polynomial gcd with endpoint checks proves all 12 and only those 12 smooth over algebraic closure. Field-trace projective point counts n=1,...,8 and Newton identities determine Frobenius characteristic polynomials because geometric Picard rank is eight for smooth degree-two del Pezzo surfaces. The attached pure Python verifier independently exhausts all coefficient vectors and repeats low-degree lifts by direct w-equation solutions. The all-n conclusion is a cohomological theorem, not extrapolation from experiments.

originality.rationale: The novel target is not existence of a Weyl type, unirationality, or single-field trace, but a complete classification of geometric smoothness, F2-isomorphism and full Picard Frobenius polynomials for all 32 quartics with the displayed fixed smooth cyclic-invariant branch conic. The compared prior work covers strictly broader existence problems or other constraints, but its statements do not imply which coefficients in this particular family realize which types. A mathematically relevant equivalent hidden coordinate description remains a risk.
residual_risks: Historical Weyl-group tables and specialized characteristic-two automorphism classifications may contain an equivalent coordinate-free or differently normalized classification.

value.rationale: The fixed smooth cyclic-invariant conic and full five-dimensional quartic invariant space form a mathematically natural finite moduli slice. It is nontrivial to classify geometric smoothness for all 32 coefficient vectors and distinguish their four arithmetic isomorphism classes. The full Frobenius polynomials and arithmetic Picard ranks separate equal rational point counts and explain Geiser-twist effects. This is a complete finite-field classification, not a routine single-example point count.
